# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003), [v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>; Mrs. Irving  <sub>[v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mother Lavendar  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>

## Appearance

Lavendar is a little lady with snow-white, thick, and wavy hair arranged in puffs and coils. Beneath her hair, she has an almost girlish, pink-cheeked face with dimples and sweet lips. She possesses large, soft wood-brown eyes containing golden glints.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Lavendar is an imaginative and romantic soul who copes with life's loneliness by pretending things and playing at imaginary scenarios. She is extremely sweet-natured, hospitable, and warm, possessing a youthful spirit that allows her to connect deeply with younger people. She is also a good, attentive listener who enjoys quiet, beautiful surroundings.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051)_

## Traits

- imaginative  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>
- hospitable  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058)</sub>
- youthful in spirit  <sub>[v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>

## History

Lavendar lived a quiet, secluded life at Echo Lodge, where she employed a young handmaiden whom she called Charlotta the Fourth. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry visited her, quickly forming a close bond over tea and shared imagination. After meeting Stephen Irving's son Paul, Lavendar formed a fond friendship with him and later reconnected with Stephen himself. The long-separated couple reconciled and were married in a late August ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor. Following their wedding, Lavendar relocated with Stephen, Paul, and Charlotta the Fourth, later settling into their new home where she remained perfectly happy.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c29 P4](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0004), [v2 c30 P0](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0000), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar because her father loved the scent after falling in love with her mother in a lavender-scented guest room  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Her mother planted the lavender borders in her garden long ago  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Lived alone at Echo Lodge after her mother passed away ten years prior  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Hired young Bowman girls starting with Charlotta the First to stay with her for board and clothes  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Was engaged to Stephen Irving twenty-five years ago before a quarrel separated them  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>

## Quotes

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can’t be silly when you want to, and when it doesn’t hurt anybody? A person must have some compensations. I don’t believe I could live at times if I didn’t pretend things.  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> I don’t care what people think about me if they don’t let me see it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

> Father named me Lavendar because he was so fond of it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
